aiRules.title: 能解釋自己的過程
aiRules.body: 說得出你怎麼問、怎麼改、為什麼這樣決定。
aiRules.bodyLong: 當老師或助教詢問時，你要能清楚說出你怎麼對 AI 提問、怎麼修改它的輸出、為什麼這樣決定。

aiRules.title: 會查證 AI 的輸出
aiRules.body: AI 會錯也會編；交出去前你要查過。
aiRules.bodyLong: AI 會犯錯，也會編造不存在的事實。交出去之前，你必須親自核對。多個 AI 講法一致，只代表這個假設值得優先查，不能取代證據。

aiRules.title: 守學術誠信與安全底線
aiRules.body: 遵守誠信、隱私與著作權；只用公開或合成資料。
aiRules.bodyLong: 遵守誠信、隱私與著作權。課堂只用公開或合成資料，不輸入個資、真實成績、私人信件或未授權的照片與聲音。把 AI 當成一起完成作品的夥伴，而不是替你寫作業的人。

aiRules.title: 不必問可不可以用
aiRules.body: 這門課就是在學怎麼用 AI；要學的是用得對，課堂上帶。
aiRules.bodyLong: 這是一門講 AI 的課，每一週的成果都預設你會用它，所以這裡不會有一張「可以／不可以」的清單。要學的是用得對：怎麼把要求講清楚、什麼時候要把它給的東西退回去、哪一句要自己查過才敢寫進報告。這件事在課堂上一堂一堂帶，另外三條守則就是底線。

intro.aiRulesNote: 前兩條 bodyLong＝陳文盛 核定 2026-06-12（D 案 4–6，第 6 條軟化版）；2026-08-26 依 v4 第三節資料底線與第五節「一致不等於證據」補寫第二、三條；投影片用 body、HTML 版可用 bodyLong。2026-09-02 陳文盛 決定：本課不列「可以／需註明／禁止」三分類例子——課程本身就是在學怎麼用 AI，怎麼用得對由授課教師在課堂帶；原 aiPolicyExamples（三分類＋pending 佔位）與英文鏡像的 aiPolicyStructure 一併移除，改補第四張卡。此決定取代 2026-06-12（D 案 7）的三分類架構在本課的適用。

faq.q: 不會寫程式、沒碰過命令列，可以修嗎？
faq.a: 可以。這門課零先修，不要求程式設計、Git 或命令列背景。你從做出有趣又有用的東西開始，再學會怎麼把任務交給 AI、預覽它要做的動作、檢查結果。
faq.source: v4 課程計畫第二節、第九節第 7 點

faq.q: 要辦帳號、付費或把作品公開嗎？
faq.a: 付費一律不用：不要求 API key、付費方案、命令列或電話驗證。帳號有三個請在課前辦好——GitHub、agent 桌面 app（二擇一）、一個聊天型 AI（見「開學前要先準備什麼？」）；這些不計分，辦不成有等值路徑、不扣一分。公開作品只有第 4 週的 GitHub Pages 練習用公開 repo＋合成內容、當堂教撤下；不想公開改看教師示範站，同分。學校帳號用來登入 e學苑交作業、Zuvio 點名，不是額外註冊也不要錢。
faq.source: course-plan.md 定案版 v5 §9-1 課前準備＋§9-2 等值路線＋§四-1 W4 Pages（Ted 8/28 裁決；2026-09-01 對齊）

faq.q: 要修完外部的 AI 線上課、交證書嗎？
faq.a: 不用。Claude Academy 與 OpenAI Academy 只當教師備課來源與學生自選延伸，不計分、不收證書，也不收帳號截圖，更不會疊在課內三小時之外。
faq.source: v4 課程計畫第九節第 1 點、第十四節

faq.q: 一定要用某個牌子的 AI 工具嗎？
faq.a: 不用。條件式工具不是共同核心。你用學校核可的工具、教師預生成的內容或完全離線的路徑，只要留下同等的作品與證據，就用同一份評分標準評分；沒用那個產品不會扣分。
faq.source: v4 課程計畫第五節末段、第十節工具分級

faq.q: 作業量大概多少？
faq.a: 作業佔總成績 20%，依教學進度與教材安排，不預設每週都有；內容、次數與繳交方式於課堂及 e學苑公告。平時成績 10% 看出席與課堂學習紀錄。
faq.source: v4 課程計畫第八節「平時 10%」「作業 20%」

faq.q: 期中怎麼評？範圍到哪裡？
faq.a: 期中佔 30%，形式是期中 AI 作品展，範圍＝第 2–7 週的能力；W1 導覽與第 8 週多模態都不考。你帶一件改良過的作品、具名可驗證的改良證據，以及一張個人判斷卡。第 8 週的多模態作品可以用來加強展示，但不是必考。
faq.source: v4 課程計畫第八節「期中 30%」

faq.q: 期末作品長什麼樣子？
faq.a: 期末佔 40%，是一個 AI 工作流專題：至少整合一項主要與一項輔助的 AI 能力、三筆測試，以及一次失敗與復原。可以沿用並深化前面幾週的作品，不要求兩套全新工具；技術難度、付費工具與公開部署本身不加分。課堂會展示過去學期的優秀作品當參考。

exampleAssets.note: 過去學期優秀作品的去識別化素材由 陳文盛 提供後嵌入

faq.source: v4 課程計畫第八節「期末 40%」＋陳文盛 定 2026-06-12（每學期末選優秀作品當下學期範例，滾動制）

faq.q: 開學前要先準備什麼？
faq.a: 照課前準備清單先弄四樣：能打字的環境（沒筆電可用教室機）、GitHub 帳號（W4 用）、agent 桌面 app 二擇一（Antigravity 要滿 18 歲並用個人 Google 帳號，或 ChatGPT 桌面版）、一個聊天型 AI。三個提醒：裝好登入成功就停手、先別玩掉額度；Antigravity 別用學校信箱；Gemini 學生方案值得申請一次，但要綁付款方式、一年後不取消會自動收費——不申請也能修完這門課。這些都不計分、不是入場門檻，沒做完也可以來上課。
faq.source: course-plan.md 定案版 v5 §9-1 課前準備四樣＋三句警語（Ted 8/28 裁決；2026-09-01 對齊）

faq.q: 還沒選上怎麼辦？
faq.a: 本班官方限修 40 人。第一堂課先來上；加退選與加簽一律依教務處公告的方式與期限辦理——時程與規則請看上方「怎麼選課」連結的官方頁面。
faq.source: 115-1 開課資料限修人數 40；選課與加簽規則一律連教務處官方頁（Course Hub 鐵則）

faq.q: AI 可以用到什麼程度？
faq.a: 可以用 AI 學習與創作，但你要能解釋過程、會查證輸出、守誠信與安全底線。課堂只用公開或合成資料，不輸入個資、真實成績或未授權的照片與聲音。
faq.source: 教學計畫守則三條＋v4 課程計畫第三節資料底線

1142-ai-intro-01.title: WCMD: An MCP Server That Lets AI Operate Windows
1142-ai-intro-01.summary: Built their own MCP Server in a week with Roo Code and DeepSeek, letting an AI agent read the screen, recognise UI elements, and drive the mouse and keyboard on its own. The result is published openly on GitHub.

1142-ai-intro-02.title: A Feature-Story Website Built with an AI Agent: The Terroir of a Jar of Plum Wine
1142-ai-intro-02.summary: Fed 25 days of brewing journals, photos, and tasting notes to Codex, then had the AI read the files and write the pages—building from scratch the feature-story website that was due for another course, and actually putting it online with a public address.

1142-ai-intro-03.title: Gemini as a Thesis-Writing Assistant
1142-ai-intro-03.summary: Brought AI into their own real thesis research: thematic analysis of interview transcripts, translating and keeping track of English-language sources, and APA format checking—plus a one-week working schedule and a first-hand account of what held up and what did not.

1142-ai-intro-04.title: Smart Beverage-Shop Inventory Management and AI Forecasting System
1142-ai-intro-04.summary: Interviewed several real bubble-tea shops first, then used Claude to build an inventory and forecasting system from scratch in a week—a Python back end with a web front end—and finally read their own development experience back against theories of human–AI collaboration.

intro.promise: From creative AI tools to supervised AI agents

destination.title: Where this course leads: an AI workflow you stay in control of
destination.sub: Not memorizing tool names—turning a real problem into work you can build, evidence, and control.

steps.label: Make something
steps.sub: Images, audio, short video, data stories, a local web app—make something first.

steps.label: Verify and test
steps.sub: Take every claim back to an original or official source; use tests to find errors, bias, fake sources, and overreach.

steps.label: Supervise and recover
steps.sub: Preview what the agent proposes, then approve, reject, or stop—and recover when it goes wrong.

phases.title: AI foundations and making
phases.body: Midterm scope = the skills of Weeks 2–7. Tell an AI tool from a teammate, a workflow, and an agent; make images, a first web app, version safety, data and bias, source-grounded research. Week 8 is multimodal work, Week 9 the midterm gallery.

phases.title: Agent literacy and supervision
phases.body: What actually counts as an agent; task contracts, action previews, permissions, dry-runs, logs, read-back, and recovery; agent-assisted data analysis and the limits of connecting to outside systems.

phases.title: Capstone and maker festival
phases.body: Turn those skills into one piece of work: a task contract, two iterations, sources and tests, red-teaming and repair, then an evidence board and your own AI-collaboration rules at the festival.

intro.phasesNote: No prerequisites—no programming, Git, or command-line background required. Every week runs Make → Test/Break → Make it yours.
weeklyPlan: Course introduction & orientation (activity: is this AI a tool, a teammate, a workflow, or an agent?)
AI sound, video, and multimodal storytelling
Midterm AI maker gallery · Weeks 2–7 skills
What makes a real AI agent?
intro.weeklyPlanNote: The weekly topics are the shared master for both sections. Product names are a living layer—rechecked the week before term starts; the capabilities and the grading standard do not change with them.

grading.label: Participation
grading.sub: Five in-class evidence cards, 2% each (AB: Weeks 2, 4, 7, 10, 14; AA: the Week-4 card moves to the merged Week-5 session); if you miss a class you may submit equivalent work for the same skill

grading.label: Assignments
grading.sub: Four kinds at 5% each: creative media, models and evidence, data and agent supervision, interaction and versions

grading.label: Midterm
grading.sub: Midterm AI maker gallery · scope = the skills of Weeks 2–7: prompting and image judgment, first web app, version safety, data and bias, source-grounded research. Week 1 (orientation) and Week 8 multimodal are not examined (multimodal may strengthen your display)

grading.label: Final
grading.sub: AI workflow project: problem and audience, the work plus two iterations, sources and tests, human control and AI disclosure, individual contribution and reflection

intro.gradingNote: The final is an AI workflow project: combine at least one primary and one supporting AI capability, three tests, and one failure with a recovery. You may extend and deepen earlier work—two brand-new tools are not required. Brand count, technical difficulty, and public deployment earn no extra credit on their own.

items.name: Text and image generation
items.sub: Turn an idea into a showable first draft, then accept, revise, or reject it yourself

items.name: Sound, video, and multimodal
items.sub: A three-shot short piece with captions and alt text, labelled for AI involvement, sources, and licence

items.name: Source-grounded research
items.sub: Claim — source — verdict card: it only counts once you reach an official, original, or trustworthy source

items.name: Data stories
items.sub: Clean, chart, and summarise a small synthetic dataset, checking at least two raw values by hand

items.name: Version safety (Git/GitHub)
items.sub: v0 → diff → approve or reject → v1; break it on purpose and still recover. No commands to memorise, no public repo

items.name: Task contract
items.sub: Outcome, how it will be verified, limits, boundaries, iteration rules, and stop conditions on one card

items.name: Action preview and permissions
items.sub: Dry-run, approve or reject, log, read-back, and restore—the human makes the final call

intro.toolGroupsNote: Tools change, skills don't—you are graded on the task, the evidence, permissions, verification, and recovery, never on a product's interface or its commands. Conditional tools (school-approved chat or image tools, NotebookLM, Canva, Sheets, and the like) are not the shared core: not using one costs you nothing.

aiRules.title: Explain your own process
aiRules.body: When the instructor or a TA asks, you should be able to say clearly how you prompted the AI, how you revised its output, and why you decided that way.

aiRules.title: Verify what AI gives you
aiRules.body: AI gets things wrong and invents facts that do not exist. Check it yourself before you hand anything in. Several models agreeing only raises the priority of a hypothesis worth checking—it does not replace evidence.

aiRules.title: Integrity and safety limits
aiRules.body: Honour academic integrity, privacy, and copyright. This course uses public or synthetic data only—no personal data, real grades, private correspondence, or unlicensed photos and audio. Treat AI as a partner in making the work, not as someone who does your assignment for you.

aiRules.title: You do not need to ask whether AI is allowed
aiRules.body: This is a course about AI. Every week assumes you will use it, so there is no list here of what is and is not allowed. What you have to learn is how to use it well: how to state what you want, when to send its output back, and which sentence you must check yourself before it goes into a report. We work through that in class, week by week. The other three rules are the floor.

intro.showcaseNote: These were the directions last term's students chose to push in—they are not a pass mark for this course and they are not a way to earn extra credit. A public repository, a live URL, and the command line are all outside what is asked of you. Grading looks only at the task, the evidence, permissions, verification, and recovery.
whatToBring: A laptop or tablet (laptop recommended); without a device, paper and pre-generated materials carry equal weight

faq.q: Can I take this without programming or command-line experience?
faq.a: Yes. There are no prerequisites: no programming, Git, or command-line background is required. You start by making something useful and interesting, then learn how to hand a task to AI, preview what it proposes, and check the result.

faq.q: Do I need an account, a paid plan, or a public portfolio?
faq.a: Payment: never—no API key, paid plan, command line, or phone verification. Accounts: three are worth setting up before term—GitHub, one agent desktop app, and one chat AI (see "What should I prepare before term starts?"); none are graded, and equivalent paths cost you nothing if they fall through. The only public artifact is the Week-4 GitHub Pages exercise, done in a public repo with synthetic content and taken down in class; if you'd rather not publish, follow the instructor's demo site for the same credit. Your university account signs you into e-Learning for submissions and Zuvio for roll call—not an extra sign-up, and it costs nothing.

faq.q: Do I have to finish an external AI course or hand in a certificate?
faq.a: No. Claude Academy and OpenAI Academy are only a source for the instructor's preparation and optional extension for you. They are not graded, no certificate or account screenshot is collected, and they are never stacked on top of the three class hours.

faq.q: Am I required to use a particular brand of AI tool?
faq.a: No. Conditional tools are not the shared core. Use a school-approved tool, instructor-generated material, or a fully offline path—as long as you leave equivalent work and evidence, the same rubric applies, and not using a given product costs you no marks.

faq.q: How much homework is there?
faq.a: Assignments are 20% of the grade, in four kinds at 5% each: creative media, models and evidence, data and agent supervision, interaction and versions. You choose one piece per kind from the listed weeks. On top of that, five in-class evidence cards make up the 10% participation grade and are completed during class.

faq.q: How is the midterm assessed, and what does it cover?
faq.a: The midterm is 30% and takes the form of a midterm AI maker gallery whose scope is the skills of Weeks 2–7 (Week 1 orientation and Week 8 multimodal are not examined). You bring one improved piece of work, attributable and verifiable evidence of the improvement, and a personal judgment card. Week 8 multimodal work may strengthen your display, but it is not examined.

faq.q: What does the final project look like?
faq.a: The final is 40%: an AI workflow project combining at least one primary and one supporting AI capability, three tests, and one failure with a recovery. You may extend and deepen work from earlier weeks—two brand-new tools are not required, and technical difficulty, paid tools, or public deployment earn no extra credit on their own. Selected work from previous terms is shown in class for reference.

faq.q: What should I prepare before term starts?
faq.a: Follow the pre-course checklist and set up four things: a typing-friendly setup (classroom PCs are available if you have no laptop), a GitHub account (used in Week 4), one agent desktop app (Antigravity needs a personal Google account and age 18+; otherwise the ChatGPT desktop app), and one chat AI. Three reminders: once installed and signed in, stop—don't burn your quota early; use a personal Google account for Antigravity, not your school email; the Gemini student plan is worth one application, but it requires a payment method and auto-renews after a year—you can finish this course without it. None of this is graded or a gate; you can attend Week 1 without it.

faq.q: What if I did not get a place in the course?
faq.a: This section has an official cap of 40 students. Come to the first class; adding and dropping, including instructor consent, follow the methods and deadlines announced by the Office of Academic Affairs—please check the official page linked under "How to enrol" above for the schedule and rules.

faq.q: How far can I go in using AI?
faq.a: You may learn and create with AI, but you must be able to explain your process, verify its output, and hold the integrity and safety limits. This course uses public or synthetic data only—no personal data, real grades, or unlicensed photos and audio.
